title: EFC — Master Formal Specification
description: The master specification for Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC), defining the complete theoretical framework comprising a dynamical sector (EFC-D) and a structural sector (EFC-S). It derives expansion, rotation curves, lensing, and structure formation from a scalar energy-flow field coupled to an entropy field, eliminating the need for dark matter and dark energy as separate components.

energy_flow_field.description: The scalar energy-flow field aligns to leading order with the negative entropy gradient, encoding energy transport along entropy-driven channels.

effective_potential.description: Effective potential coupling energy flow and entropy, with amplitude A_Φ and coupling exponent β (baseline β=1).

expansion_rate.description: Effective expansion rate derived from the magnitude of energy flow and thermodynamic modulation by entropy, producing late-time acceleration without dark energy.

rotation_velocity.description: Circular velocity from the gradient of the effective potential; flat rotation curves emerge from the coupled entropy-energy landscape without dark matter.

effective_light_speed.description: Entropy-dependent effective speed of light, with normalized entropy coordinate x(S) = (S − S_mid)/(ΔS/2), producing focusing at low entropy and defocusing at high entropy.

light_travel_time.description: Observed light-travel time integrated along the photon path through the variable-c(S) medium.

key_results.main_finding: A unified thermodynamic framework in which expansion, rotation curves, lensing, and structure formation all emerge from a scalar energy-flow field Ef coupled to an entropy field S, without invoking dark matter or dark energy.

sealed_predictions.statement: Mid-entropy regions (S ≈ S_mid) produce maximum light-travel-time delays due to c(S) reaching its minimum there, generating a distinctive delay-versus-entropy signature in lensing time delays.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Strong-lensing time-delay measurements showing no correlation between inferred entropy environment and delay residuals.

sealed_predictions.statement: Flat rotation curves emerge from the entropy-flow potential gradient without a dark-matter halo; the predicted v(r) profile tracks ∂Φ/∂r shaped by the local entropy landscape.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Galaxy rotation-curve fits requiring an additional mass component beyond the EFC entropy-potential prediction at >5σ across a representative sample.

sealed_predictions.statement: Late-time cosmic acceleration arises from evolution of (Ef, S) without a cosmological constant, predicting a specific H(z) trajectory tied to entropy evolution.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Precision H(z) measurements (e.g., DESI BAO) inconsistent with any realizable (Ef, S) trajectory at >5σ.

kill_criteria: KC1: Rotation-curve data across diverse galaxy morphologies cannot be fit by the entropy-potential gradient ∂Φ/∂r without introducing an additional dark-matter-like component (>5σ residuals in a representative sample).
KC2: Precision H(z) measurements (BAO, SNe Ia) are inconsistent with any physical trajectory of (Ef, S) in the EFC expansion-rate formula at >5σ.
KC3: Strong-lensing time delays show no dependence on the inferred entropy environment, contradicting the c(S) variation prediction.
KC4: Laboratory or astrophysical bounds exclude any detectable variation of the effective speed of light c(S) at the level required by EFC's a_edge parameter.
KC5: CMB power-spectrum features (acoustic peaks, damping tail) cannot be reproduced by the EFC entropy-field framework without reintroducing standard ΛCDM components.
